types.name: ProcessEngagement
types.doc:
What engages a process before its path and disengages it after: motion-program operations that run around the
process span, and that a restart runs again, since each restart re-engages. A welder strikes its arc and waits for
it to establish before the torch travels (`entry`), and fills the crater, ends the wire and the arc after (`exit`);
a sprayer or a dispenser needs neither, and has none.

`entry` runs once the tool stands at the start of the span, so its outputs fire there; barriers such as a dwell
or an input wait may follow them. `exit` runs once the path is done, with the tool still at its end.

With an `exit`, the process outputs the path's events drive are not zeroed at the path's end: the exit does that,
in its own order, and the run ends when its caller says the program is done (`ProcessRun.finish`) rather than when
the path is. Without one, the run ends at the path's end, and the process output goes to zero there.

types.name: WeldCorner
types.doc:
How the torch turns where one weld segment meets the next at an angle (a corner of a tube, the sides of a post). The
turn is part of the travel: the torch turns half of the way on the last stretch of one segment and half on the first
stretch of the next, at the travel speed, so the wire feed that keeps the deposit per length constant stays right and no
metal piles up where the torch would otherwise stand still to turn.

The length of the turn comes from the arm and the angle, not from a constant. The torch must reorient by the angle `a`
between the two segments' orientations while the tip keeps its travel speed `v`, and the wrist can turn the torch at no
more than `HEADROOM` of its angular speed `w` and acceleration `α` (the rest is for the wrist's share of moving the tip).
A rest-to-rest turn of `a` under those limits takes

T = a / w' + w' / α'   if a ≥ w'² / α'   (the speed limit is reached),
T = 2 · sqrt(a / α')   otherwise          (it is not),

with w' = HEADROOM · w and α' = HEADROOM · α, and the tip travels `v · T` while it does, half of it on each side of the
corner. A sharper corner is a longer turn; a straight join (no change of orientation) has none. The length is kept within
`MIN_TURN` and `MAX_TURN` so that a sensible turn is never smeared along a whole seam or shorter than the path can
follow, and what a segment gives to a corner is at most `SHARE` of its own length.

types.name: WeldPathPlanner
types.doc:
Plans a weld for an arm before it runs: which roll of the torch about its wire each segment is welded at, and how the
torch comes in and leaves, so that every pose of the motion is reachable and the torch and arm are clear of the work.

A seam's frame fixes the wire (the work and travel angles) and, by its +X along the travel, also the torch's roll about
the wire: the swan neck leads. That roll does not matter to the weld, but it decides whether the arm can hold the pose
and what the neck and the arm come near, and the sides of a tube, with the travel turning a quarter at each corner, ask
for four different ones. So each segment is tried at the rolls in `ROLLS`, the one nearest the previous segment's first,
and also tries a roll derived from the previous orientation to avoid extra wrist twist. It takes the first at which
the arm can follow the corner into it and the segment, every `STEP` metres, without leaving
its branch, and at which `clearance` finds nothing near. If the segments after cannot be done from where that leaves the
arm, the search goes back and tries the next roll (at most `BUDGET` segment tries per entry configuration).

The first segment is entered, and the last left, along the first of these that is reachable and clear: out along the wire
by the plan's approach distance, along the open side of the corner by that distance, and both again at twice the
distance. If a joint move from where the arm stands to the entry would sweep the arm through the work, the entry is made
from over it: a joint move to `VIA_HEIGHT` above the approach pose, then straight down.

The search checks a joint-space sweep to the entry, the straight moves, the segments with their corner turns, the lift
and the retreat, sampled every `STEP` metres of the tip (and every 0.02 rad of a joint in the joint move). Where the tip is
within `CONTACT_ZONE` of the weld path the torch is held to the contact margin of the clearance, elsewhere to its margin.
`compileMotion`, when supplied, then validates the complete program and its actual joint trajectories before a candidate
is accepted. A weld no roll and no entry can do fails with the reasons: the part, its neighbour, the distance and where the tip was.

types.name: WeldingPlanRunner
types.doc:
Welds one seam with an arm: a MotionKit program, run by `ManipulatorMotion`, whose process is driven by a
`ProcessRun` over a `WelderProcessDevice`. It works through the robot alone: the torch's channels and the arm's
motion, and the welder's `tool_weld` reading, which the caller hands in each tick (`WeldSeam` takes it from the
robot's sensor), so the same runner welds on a fixed arm or a mobile base, simulated or real.

The program is: a joint move to the approach pose (`approach` out along the wire from the start), a straight move
to the start, then the process run's - the arc strikes there (voltage and wire speed set, arc on) and the program
waits on the welder's established arc, or gives the seam up after `IGNITION_TIMEOUT`; it dwells `startDwell`; the
torch follows the seam at the travel speed with the wire speed that keeps the deposit per length constant; it dwells
`craterDwell` at the end with the arc up; the wire stops and the torch lifts `LIFT` over the burnback time while the
arc, with nothing feeding it, burns back, and the arc command ends; the torch retracts to the approach pose. The
process run's engagement (`ProcessEngagement`) carries the arc and the crater.

If the welder faults mid-seam - the arc is lost, or never strikes - the process run interrupts, the arm stops, and
once the fault has cleared the run restarts `BACKOFF` metres before where it stopped, so the new bead overlaps the
old; at most `maxRestarts` times, after which the weld fails.

fields.name: pathOf
fields.doc:
The path the wire tip follows: a straight line per segment, the torch holding its orientation along it. Where
the next segment's orientation differs (a corner), the torch turns as it passes: along the last stretch of one
segment and the first of the next it turns half the way each, so that it meets the corner at the orientation midway
between the two and has the next segment's own orientation once past it. The turn is part of the travel, at the
travel speed, so the wire feed that keeps the deposit per length constant stays right, and no metal is piled
where the torch would otherwise stand still to turn. How long the stretch is comes from the angle and the wrist's
limits (`WeldCorner`), and a corner takes at most `WeldCorner.SHARE` of a segment.

types.name: FaceBridge
types.doc:
Converts a CadKit planar Face into a design WorkSurface: its outer wire
becomes the boundary, its inner wires become exclusions, all expressed
in a local plane frame built from the face's own center and normal
(`frame_T_surface`'s rotation columns are `basisU, basisV, normal`, so
the surface's local +Z is the face's outward normal, per WorkSurface's
contract). `scale` converts the shape's own linear units into meters
(CadKit itself is unit-agnostic; BimKit's convention is millimeters, so
`WallBridge` passes `scale = 0.001`).

`cadkit.Face` (haxe/src/cadkit/Face.hx) does not expose wire/vertex
enumeration, but `Face.cloneShape()` already returns a full `Shape` over
just that face, and `Shape.subshapeCount`/`subshape` already walk any
`CadKit.ShapeKind`, including `Wire` and `Vertex` — no CadKit change was
needed to read a face's boundary loops.

types.name: WallBridge
types.doc:
Converts a BimKit wall's side face into a WorkSurface. Hosted
windows/doors already cut through-holes into that face
(bimkit.BimDocument.rebuildWall boolean-cuts the wall body with every
hosted opening), so they surface as FaceBridge exclusions automatically:
one inner wire, and so one exclusion, per opening. BimKit's own
convention is millimeter dimensions (see bimkit.BimSchema quantities),
so geometry is scaled by 1/1000 into RobotKit's meters.

Shaping must be disabled during acquisition. The caller supplies this experimental fact; it is not guessed from a sweep.
Klipper's PSD CSV may be TEST_RESONANCES or SHAPER_CALIBRATE output (extra shaper columns are ignored).

types.name: HeightMapCollision
types.doc:
A `HeightMap` as a collision height field (COLLISION.md CL3a, CL-D6). The
map's vertices run along +x by column and +y by row from its origin; a
collision height field is centred on its offset with rows along -y, so
rows are flipped and the offset is the map's centre in its frame.

The field is a solid down to `floor`, which must lie below the deepest
dig: the world refuses heights below it rather than clamp them.

fields.name: offset
fields.doc: The field's offset in the map's frame: its centre.

fields.name: heights
fields.doc: The heights in the field's layout (rows along -y), for `CollisionWorld.setHeights` after digging.

fields.name: describe
fields.doc:
Adds the terrain as a fixed body at `framePose` (the map frame's pose in
the cell) in `group`; returns the described object.

types.name: ReachabilityChecker
types.doc:
For one candidate base placement (folded into `base_T_work`, the
manipulator chain's base frame to the toolpath's own frame), solves IK for
every point of a `Toolpath` segment, seeded by continuation from the
previous point, and reports the reachable fraction rather than aborting
at the first failure.

fields.name: solveApproach
fields.doc:
Solves the pose a tool starts a path from, with the arm at `seed`. That pose is far from the seed (the arm unfolds from its
rest posture to the work), which is what the reaching method is for: tracking steps from a nearby seed, and from here it
can stall at a joint limit or wind a joint a full turn to the same pose, depending on millimetres of base error. Planning
(`check`) and running a plan (`SurfacePlanRunner`) both solve it here, so the one that calls a pose reachable is the one
that reaches it.

types.name: ReachabilityResult
types.doc:
Outcome of `ReachabilityChecker.check`: the fraction of a `Toolpath`'s
points a `Manipulator` could reach from one base placement, the index of
the first unreachable point (`-1` if every point converged), and the
final joint solution attempted (converged or not), so a caller can seed a
following check with it.

types.name: WorkPatch
types.doc: One planned patch: its own sub-`WorkSurface`, raster `Toolpath`, and the base pose it is reachable from.

types.name: WorkPatchPlanResult
types.doc: The ordered patch plan; `fullyPlanned` is false if any patch could not reach 100% from any searched candidate.

types.name: WorkPatchPlanner
types.doc:
Splits a `WorkSurface` into axis-aligned column patches (no wider than
`maxPatchWidth`, mirroring `RasterToolpathGenerator`'s axis-aligned
scope), builds a raster `Toolpath` per patch, and searches a grid of
candidate base placements — in front of the wall, in a fixed standoff
band, facing the wall, at least `clearance` from the authored obstacles — to
find one from which the whole patch toolpath is reachable
(`ReachabilityChecker`). Base motion between the returned patches is the
existing planar `Navigator`/`GoTo`, driven by each patch's `basePose`;
this planner does no joint base+arm optimization.

types.name: ModbusFrame
types.doc: Modbus TCP MBAP framing; register words are big endian.

types.name: ModbusFrameStream
types.doc: Bounded TCP reassembly; a receive can split or coalesce MBAP records.

types.name: ModbusRegister
types.doc: One unsigned holding/input register, with engineering units = raw * scale + offset.

types.name: ModbusTcpClient
types.doc: Nonblocking, single-transaction Modbus TCP client, polled by the process owner.

fields.name: discardQueued
fields.doc: Discard unsent setpoints before a process stop; the in-flight transaction still has an acknowledgement.

types.name: ModbusWelder

fields.name: faultDetail
fields.doc: Adapter diagnostics supplement the device-neutral, frozen tool sensor fault codes.

types.name: ModbusWelderMap
types.doc: Vendor register addresses/scales and bit assignments; no addresses belong in the driver.

fields.name: leaseAddress
fields.doc: The device expires its output lease even if TCP cannot deliver a final arc-off write.

types.name: ConfigInstaller
types.doc:
Puts a `printer.cfg` on a machine and finds out what Klipper made of it: uploads it to Moonraker's config root,
restarts the firmware (`printer/firmware_restart`), waits for Klippy to come back, reads the configuration it is running and
compares that with the file (see `ConfigReadback`). Polled with the client by whoever owns the clock; `mismatches` is
set when `done`.

fields.name: mismatches
fields.doc: What differs between the file and the running configuration, or why Klippy did not come back; empty when they agree.

fields.name: interval
fields.doc: Seconds between asks after the restart, and how long Klippy has to be ready again.

fields.name: new
fields.doc: `expected` is the file as sections and keys (the caller's own parser reads it).

fields.name: start
fields.doc: Begins: the upload goes out with the client's next turn.

types.name: ConfigReadback
types.doc:
Compares a Klipper configuration as written with the one Klipper reports running (`configfile.settings` and
`configfile.warnings`). Klipper lower-cases keys and returns numbers and booleans as such, and adds defaults for what the
file leaves out; only what the file says is compared. A pin that is still a placeholder is for the user to replace, so a
caller passes the text it actually uploaded.

fields.name: TOLERANCE
fields.doc: Relative tolerance of two numbers: Klipper reads a decimal and writes a double.

fields.name: compare
fields.doc: The differences, each a sentence: a section or key the machine does not have, a value that differs, a warning Klipper gave.

types.name: HttpResponse
types.doc: A response: status, headers and body.

fields.name: reason
fields.doc: Empty when the HTTP backend does not expose a reason phrase (for example HTTP/2).

types.name: MoonrakerClient
types.doc:
A nonblocking Moonraker client over NativeKit's HTTP backend, polled by whoever owns the clock (the application's
frame, a test's loop). One request is in flight at a time; the rest wait their
turn. A transport failure, a reply that does not come within `timeout` seconds, an error status or a body that is
not what the request asked for is the client's `fault`, and ends it: a machine that answers wrongly is to be
reconnected to, not argued with.

fields.name: sentBytes
fields.doc: Application body bytes submitted (wire headers are owned by the HTTP backend).

fields.name: idle
fields.doc: Nothing is in flight or waiting.

fields.name: send
fields.doc: Sends a request with no body when the ones before it have been answered.

fields.name: sendBody
fields.doc: Sends a request with a body of `contentType` (none when null) when the ones before it have been answered.

fields.name: status
fields.doc: What the machine is doing now.

fields.name: serverInfo
fields.doc: The server's own information (Klippy's state among it), as Moonraker's `result`.

fields.name: upload
fields.doc: Puts `content` in the gcodes as `filename`, and starts printing it when `print` is set. Calls back with the stored path.

fields.name: uploadTo
fields.doc: Puts `content` in one of Moonraker's file roots (`gcodes`, `config`) as `filename`. Calls back with the stored path.

fields.name: downloadFile
fields.doc: Read an explicitly published artifact. Klipper's /tmp is not a Moonraker file root.

fields.name: script
fields.doc: Runs G-code or a Klipper command on the machine.

fields.name: firmwareRestart
fields.doc:
Restarts the firmware so it reads its configuration again. Moonraker's own endpoint, not `FIRMWARE_RESTART` as a
script: Klippy goes away while the script runs, so the script's request ends in an error even when the restart works.

fields.name: runningConfig
fields.doc: The configuration Klipper is running: `settings` (section to key to value, as it parsed them) and its `warnings`.

fields.name: start
fields.doc: Starts printing a file already in the gcodes.

fields.name: poll
fields.doc: Moves the conversation on: reads what has arrived, answers the request in flight and sends the next.

types.name: MoonrakerHeater
types.doc: One heater as Moonraker reports it, degrees Celsius.

types.name: MoonrakerSocket
types.doc:
Moonraker's JSON-RPC WebSocket, on NativeKit's message transport and polled by whoever owns the clock. After the opening
handshake it subscribes (`printer.objects.subscribe`) to the objects `MoonrakerStatus` reads: Moonraker answers with
their state and then pushes `notify_status_update` with the fields that changed, each of which is merged into the state
kept here, so a twin is told the moment the machine reports instead of when it next asks. A handshake or a call that is
not answered within `timeout` seconds, a malformed frame or a close from the server is the socket's `fault`, and ends it.

fields.name: onUpdate
fields.doc: Called with the machine's state each time the subscription answers or pushes an update.

fields.name: status
fields.doc: The latest state, once the subscription has answered.

fields.name: updates
fields.doc: How many updates have arrived (the answer to the subscription counts), and the clock of the latest.

fields.name: subscribe
fields.doc: Asks for the objects `MoonrakerStatus` reads once the socket is open; updates follow on their own.

fields.name: call
fields.doc: Calls a JSON-RPC method (sent when the socket opens, if it has not yet).

fields.name: poll
fields.doc: Moves the conversation on: the handshake, the calls waiting to go out, and every message that has arrived.

types.name: MoonrakerStatus
types.doc:
What a Klipper machine reports through Moonraker (`printer/objects/query`, or the `printer.objects.subscribe`
updates over the WebSocket): where the toolhead is, the heaters and the state of the print. Lengths are the machine's,
millimetres.

The toolhead's position comes from `motion_report.live_position`, where the nozzle is now. `toolhead.position` is the
end of the last move queued, which runs ahead of the nozzle by everything Klipper has planned but not yet stepped (a
fraction of a second to seconds); it is kept apart as `queuedPosition` and a twin must not follow it.

fields.name: state
fields.doc: `standby`, `printing`, `paused`, `complete`, `cancelled` or `error`.

fields.name: progress
fields.doc: Fraction of the file printed, 0 to 1.

fields.name: position
fields.doc: The nozzle's x, y and z and the extruder's position now (`motion_report.live_position`).

fields.name: velocity
fields.doc: The toolhead's speed and the extruder's, millimetres per second (`live_velocity`, `live_extruder_velocity`).

fields.name: queuedPosition
fields.doc: Where the last queued move ends (`toolhead.position`): ahead of `position`.

fields.name: QUERY
fields.doc: The same asked of an HTTP `printer/objects/query`.

fields.name: new
fields.signature: (state:String, filename:String, progress:Float, position:Array<Float>, velocity:Float, extruderVelocity:Float, queuedPosition:Array<Float>, extruder:MoonrakerHeater, bed:MoonrakerHeater, message:String):Void

fields.name: subscription
fields.doc: The objects and fields that `fromObjects` reads, as a subscription (`null` fields would mean all of an object's).

fields.name: fromObjects
fields.doc:
Reads the `status` object of a query reply or the merged state of a subscription. What the machine left out keeps its
value in `previous` (the last status read), or is zero or empty when there is none: a field that is not in a reply is not
a reading of zero.

fields.name: parse
fields.doc: Reads a reply to `QUERY`; a malformed reply is refused.

types.name: ToolpathPosePath
types.doc: Converts RobotKit authoring points into a framed MotionKit process path.

types.name: Toolpath
types.doc:
An ordered sequence of `ToolpathPoint`s expressed in one named frame
(`frameId`; a `WorkSurface` frame, or any other frame a `FrameTree3` can
resolve into the manipulator's base frame). Points may be empty only for
a segment produced by `segmentByProcess`.

fields.name: length
fields.doc: Sum of straight-line distances between consecutive points.

fields.name: processOnLength
fields.doc:
Sum of straight-line distances for moves whose *departing* point has
`processOn == true` (the point's process state governs the move to the
next point).

fields.name: segmentByProcess
fields.doc:
Splits into a leading `approach` run (processOn == false), the middle
`process` run from the first to the last processOn == true point
inclusive, and a trailing `retract` run. If no point has processOn ==
true, `approach` holds every point and `process`/`retract` are empty.

types.name: ToolpathPoint
types.doc:
One waypoint of a `Toolpath`: a TCP pose expressed in the toolpath's own
frame (`work_T_tcp`, following `a_T_b`), the feed rate for the move that
reaches it, whether the tool process is on for that move, and an optional
desired surface normal/standoff a generator may attach for downstream use
(e.g. reachability or coverage checks).

types.name: ToolpathSegments
types.doc: Result of `Toolpath.segmentByProcess`; each part shares the source toolpath's frame.

types.name: ContactMeasurement
types.doc: One fresh contact observation, with the clock and coordinate facts used by registration.

fields.name: new
fields.signature: (sensorId:String, sensorFrame:String, sensorKind:String, coordinateFrame:String, sequence:Int64, sourceTimestampNs:Int64, sourceClockId:String, jointTimestampNs:Int64, clockErrorNs:Int64, point:Vec3, uncertaintyMeters:Float):Void

types.name: ContactPoseEnvelope
types.doc:
Set-valued contact registration. A bounded chassis-pose error transforms measured points back into
the nominal chassis frame. Interval constraints retain every pose consistent with calibrated
contact error; a search budget may leave wider boxes, never silently remove unknown components.
Euler intervals are restricted to +/-90 degrees so their sine ranges are monotone.

fields.name: translationBound
fields.doc: Component-wise chassis error bounds from the saved registration request.

fields.name: fork
fields.doc: Independent planning branch with the same conservative pose set.

fields.name: containsWorkFrame
fields.doc: True only when a candidate satisfies the authored root bounds and every retained plane observation.

fields.name: constrainWorkFrame
fields.doc: Clamp a noisy point-to-plane fit to authored root bounds, then prove it against every observation.

fields.name: maximumPlaneResidual
fields.doc: Largest direct residual against the retained source observations for a candidate work frame.

fields.name: describeWorkFrame
fields.doc: Explain a rejected provisional fit without treating its marginal ranges as authorization.

fields.name: refine
fields.doc: Refine with all observations collected so far. Unsupported poses or inconsistent observations fail explicitly.

fields.name: estimate
fields.doc: A provisional centre for placing probes; this never authorizes welding or discards the set-valued bounds.

fields.name: region
fields.doc: Bound the actual work-frame intersection of a probe placed using the current provisional estimate.

types.name: ContactRegionBounds
types.doc: Conservative bounds of a search ray's intersection with its nominal CAD plane, in metres.

types.name: ContactRegistration
types.doc: Rigid point-to-plane registration. Inputs contain observations, never a live work-body pose.

types.name: ContactRegistrationPrecision
types.doc: Allocate a rigid-registration error budget over a measured 3-2-1 pattern and its work extent.

fields.name: contactError
fields.doc: Smaller patterns need finer contacts; near-parallel planes also consume the pose-error budget.

types.name: ContactRegistrationResult
types.doc: An incomplete estimate may guide another probe, but only an accepted frame can authorize welding.

types.name: ContactRegistrationSequence
types.doc: Measured 3-2-1 registration policy; selection receives only CAD/observed uncertainty, never physical work poses.

fields.name: measurements
fields.doc: Typed source observations retained with the accepted pose for downstream uncertainty checks.

fields.name: activeStage
fields.doc: The selected CAD plane and its checked probes, while the sequence works on that plane.

fields.name: selectNextStage
fields.doc: Select the next plane from completed measurements; the runner then follows its checked entry.

fields.name: observeMeasurement
fields.doc: Production observations retain sensor identity, units, frame, acquisition time and error bound.

types.name: ContactRegistrationStage
types.doc: Prepared probes on one nominal work-frame plane; all lengths are in metres.

fields.name: entryJoints
fields.doc: Checked entry posture for this stage; null uses the saved registration start.

types.name: ContactSearch
types.doc: Bounded contact probing policy. Motion and joint FK remain with the caller.

fields.name: contactOffset
fields.doc: Calibrated distance from the sensing threshold to the material, along the search direction.

fields.name: maximumOvershoot
fields.doc: Maximum measured contact travel past the nominal endpoint while fresh feedback is stopping the servo.

fields.name: observe
fields.doc: Point is measured joint FK on now's clock; the maximum sensor skew bounds contact-position error.

types.name: PlaneContact
types.doc: A nominal work-frame plane and a measured contact point in the observer frame, in metres.

types.name: SimulatedSurfaceScanner
types.doc:
Samples points from a "true" wall that differs from a design `WorkSurface`
by a small rigid offset/rotation (`surface_T_trueSurface`, e.g. +14 mm
along the surface's local +Z and a small rotation about local +Y
representing an installation yaw error) plus a smooth bow, with seeded
Gaussian-like noise. Openings (the design surface's exclusions) are
skipped, matching what a real scanner would see through a window/door.

The bow term is re-centered to zero mean over the actual sampled points
before the rigid offset is applied, so `PlaneFit`/`SurfaceRegistration`
recovers the injected offset/rotation rather than a bow-biased plane; the
bow itself remains visible as a spatial pattern in a `DeviationMap`.

fields.name: scan
fields.signature: (design:WorkSurface, surface_T_trueSurface:Transform3, bowAmplitude:Float, pointSpacing:Float, noiseStdDev:Float, seed:Int, sourceTimestampNs:Int64):PointCloud

types.name: SurfaceRegistration
types.doc:
Registers a design `WorkSurface` against an observed point cloud: fits a
plane (seeded RANSAC, robust to outliers), derives the minimal correction
transform between the design plane and the fitted plane, and — unless the
correction exceeds the configured limits — derives a corrected `work`
`WorkSurface` that carries the design surface's boundary/exclusions (their
in-plane shape is unaffected by an out-of-plane correction) at the
corrected pose, with provenance pointing back at the design element.

types.name: SurfaceRegistrationResult
types.doc:
Result of `SurfaceRegistration.register`. `correction` is the minimal
rigid transform (`surface_T_correctedSurface`) that reconciles the design
plane (`z = 0` in the surface's own frame) with the observed plane: a
rotation tilting the design's `+Z` onto the fitted normal, about the axis
`(0, 0, 1) x normal` (identity when they already agree), and a translation
of `offset` along that normal — i.e. purely out-of-plane. In-plane
shift/rotation about the normal is not observable from a plane fit alone
and is left as identity. `registered` is the corrected `work` WorkSurface
(`null` when `accepted` is false).

types.name: PressBrakeChannels

types.doc:
Discrete controller outputs with fresh measured feedback and explicit readiness.

fields.doc: Stop drive and reverse independently; preserve the held screw's vacuum.

types.name: FasteningRunReport

fields.name: skip

fields.name: installed

fields.name: resumeAfterStop

types.name: ForceGuidedScrewEntry
types.doc:
Runs a `ScrewEntryController` over a `ServoSession` on fresh force/torque samples. This side owns what the
controller does not: the robot and sensor clocks, sample freshness and ordering, the sensor-to-TCP transform, the
measured travel, force, torque and run-time hard stops, and bringing the arm to rest before reporting. The
controller is made at `start`, when the measured approach pose fixes how deep the CAD entry plane lies.

fields.name: entry
fields.doc: The CAD entry pose in the robot root: x and y span the hole plane, z advances into the hole.

fields.name: feed
fields.doc: The tool's compliant feed: its robot joint and its axis at the TCP; the measured tip includes its travel.

fields.name: regionHalfU
fields.doc: Lateral reach of the registered region around the approach axis.

fields.name: peakForceN
fields.doc: Peak measured force during this search, excluding later fastening loads.

fields.name: measuredEntry
fields.doc: The measured TCP at rest after a seated entry.

fields.name: origin
fields.doc: The measured TCP when the search started: the approach pose.

fields.name: sensorTransformAtTcp
fields.doc: `tcp_T_sensor` from the two frames' poses in their shared link.

fields.signature: (servo:ServoSession, limits:ScrewEntryLimits, admittance:CartesianAdmittance, entry:Transform3, depthTolerance:Float, sensorId:String, sensorFrame:String, tcpFromSensor:Transform3, maximumAgeNs:Int64, maximumForceN:Float, maximumTorqueNm:Float, maximumTravelMeters:Float, maximumTravelRadians:Float, maximumRunSeconds:Float, regionHalfU:Float, regionHalfV:Float, ?mappings:ClockMappings, ?feed:{joint:Int, axisAtTcp:Vec3}):Void

fields.name: update
fields.doc: Read one robot snapshot and, on a fresh force/torque sample, run one control step.

types.name: PolledScrewdriverDevice
types.doc: A nonblocking controller serviced independently of motion planning.

types.name: ScrewCollisionPolicy
types.doc: Exact thread, clamp and driver contacts from one named CAD fastening.

types.name: ScrewEntryController
types.doc:
Hybrid force/position screw entry, free of clocks, sensors and servos: measured TCP displacement and wrench in,
a TCP twist out. The advance axis `n` is force-controlled on a surface (the admittance regulates the compression
to the commissioned force) and a guarded descent while unloaded between surfaces; the hole plane (`u`, `v`) is
position-controlled.

Whenever the screw touches a surface it searches that surface with an Archimedean spiral around the lateral target,
whose parameter advances only while the tool tracks it. Dropping `entryAdvance` below the touched depth means a
hole: the screw descends again with no lateral target of its own, so the bore it is in centres it. Reaching the
CAD entry plane plus `entryAdvance`, touching or not, puts the screw in the registered hole: the tightening

How the bit carries the identified screw. Exactly one body path owns the screw at a time, and the

fields.name: Suction

Runs before the next physics step. While the arm owns axial motion the held screw is a rigid physical

is held by vacuum again at its measured pose. A physical thread engages after the mission's approach.

types.name: SimulatedWelder
types.doc:
A MIG/MAG welder on one link of a simulated robot, worked by its channels as a real supply is: the arc
(digital), the wire speed (metres per minute) and the voltage (volts). After each step it finds where the wire
tip is, asks the grounded work how far away that is, lets `WeldArcModel` say what the circuit does (see there for
the arc, the current and voltage, touch and faults) and publishes the result as one `tool_weld` frame on its
sensor, as the suction tool publishes its vacuum.

**Geometry.** The physics engine reports contacts of the robot's collision shapes, and the wire is not one of
them: it is a few millimetres of metal beyond the nozzle, and the arc strikes across a gap, which a contact
would not report. So the welder asks the work itself, in the world frame: the distance of the wire tip from
the grounded solids (`WeldWork.distance`) and a ray along the wire (`WeldWork.ray`). The work is convex solids
on the links that carry them (`GroundedWork`), so it follows them when they move.

The tip is the tool point: `tipPosition` and `wireDirection` are in the frame of the link that carries the torch
(metres), the direction being the torch's +Z, along the wire out of the nozzle.

Add it to the simulation as a step observer; it acts after each step. Its arc channel is not a `keepOnStop`
channel, so a stop or a fault takes it to its safe value, off, and the arc goes out.

fields.doc: The supply is on and healthy; clear it to model a dropout of the mains or the gas.

types.name: DigTrench
types.doc:
Digs a straight trench (`lineFrom` -> `lineTo`, `width`, `depth` below the
ground elevation sampled from `heightMap` at `start()`, `gradeTolerance`)
with `DigCyclePlanner`, one bounded pass at a time: each cycle samples the
*current* terrain from `heightMap`, cuts down by at most
`spec.maxCutPerPass` toward the trench's design elevation, executes the
cycle's `Toolpath` through validated plans, and applies the resulting
`BucketSweep` to `heightMap` directly -- so progress is always read back
from the height map (`remainingDepthError`), the way a real excavator's
only feedback is the ground it has actually moved, never the commanded
cycle alone. Stops (succeeds) once every one of `spec.progressSamples + 1`
evenly-spaced points along the line is within `gradeTolerance` of the
design elevation, or fails after `spec.maxCycles` -- a bounded operation,
not an open-ended search, per the plan. The trench's `width` becomes the
swept bucket half-width for the whole pass (a single lane), rather than
multiple side-by-side bucket passes -- the smallest correct reading of
"width" for this milestone's bounded scope; see ARCHITECTURE.md.

fields.doc: Design surface used to clamp every executed cut.

fields.name: footprint
fields.doc: Planar trench footprint used to reject sweep vertices outside the work region.

fields.doc: Dig cycles completed so far.

types.doc: Try an identified screw, recover a NOK, then use one identified replacement before reporting and moving on.

types.name: DumpAt
types.doc:
Moves the bucket to a target TCP `pose` (chain-base frame) and holds it
there -- a bounded joint move to a TCP IK target through a validated plan, the
same machinery `DigTrench`/`GradeRegion` use for their own dump legs,
exposed standalone for a caller that already holds a loaded bucket (e.g.
after a manual or externally-commanded dig) and just needs to relocate and
release. Unlike `DigTrench`/`GradeRegion`, `pose` is not required to lie
on the excavator chain's reachable orientation manifold (see
`DigCyclePlanner.poseAt`) -- a caller building one with that helper gets
an exact solve; an arbitrary pose gets the manipulator's ordinary
best-effort IK convergence.

types.doc: Measured execution and an explicitly skipped final pass expose the same reporting boundary.

types.name: FinishSpec
types.doc:
Process parameters for one `FinishSurface` run: raster geometry
(`toolWidth`/`overlap`/`standoff`/`feedRate`/`leadInOut`, the same
`RasterToolpathGenerator` inputs `WorkPatchPlanner` forwards per patch),
`maxPatchWidth`/standoff-search band for `WorkPatchPlanner`, and the
Cartesian/IK tolerances used while compiling each patch plan. A
pure-data anonymous typedef, per haxeon's structural-typing rules.

types.name: FinishSurface
types.doc:
Splits the surface into patches, navigates the base, and runs each patch
through a motion plan. Process events drive the tool adapter. Coverage is
measured from observed joint positions and the current base localization.

types.name: GradeRegion
types.doc:
Grades an `EarthworkRegion` toward its design `HeightMap`, one bounded
cycle at a time: each cycle asks `region.worstVertex()` for the
largest-magnitude, non-excluded, out-of-tolerance vertex, cuts it down by
at most `spec.maxCutPerPass` toward its design elevation with a single
`DigCyclePlanner` cycle (a degenerate zero-length "cut" segment centered on
that vertex, since a `GradeRegion` cycle targets one spot rather than a
line), executes it, and applies the resulting `BucketSweep` to
`region.existing` directly. Stops (succeeds) once `worstVertex()` returns
null, or fails after `spec.maxCycles` -- a bounded search over the
region's existing grid, not open-ended, per the plan. Only cut (existing
above design) is handled: fill/embankment is out of scope (no soil
mechanics, per the plan's explicit boundary), so a region whose worst
vertex needs fill fails explicitly rather than looping forever.

types.doc:

pass takes real time on a real sensor) then captures one `PointCloud` from
the supplied `scan` callback. `scan` carries every scanner-specific
parameter (which surface, sensor pose, noise, seed) as a closure so this
skill stays independent of any one scanning technique — a real LiDAR scan
accumulation, `processkit.perception.SimulatedSurfaceScanner.scan`, or a
replayed cloud can all be supplied the same way. `scan` must be
deterministic given the observations already available to the caller (no
wall-clock or hidden randomness), so this skill replays identically.

types.name: WeldParameters
types.doc:
How a weld is run: the arc (wire speed in metres per minute, voltage in volts), the travel speed along the path
in metres per second, and the sequence around it. The torch comes in from `approach` metres out along the wire, strikes
the arc at the start and holds until it is established, dwells `startDwell` seconds, travels the path, dwells
`craterDwell` seconds at its end to fill the crater, stops the wire, lets the arc burn back for `burnback` seconds
and goes out again.

types.name: WeldPasses
types.doc: Run each pass to completion, with cooling between passes and the arc off during that cooling.

types.name: WeldPlan
types.doc:
A weld to run: a path of segments, each starting where the one before ends (a straight seam is one segment, the four
sides of a tube four), and the parameters. The arc is struck at the start of the first segment, stays up along the
whole path and ends at the end of the last; where one segment's orientation differs from the next one's the torch
turns between them as it passes the corner.

fields.name: JOIN
fields.doc: Positions of consecutive segments this close are joined, in metres.

fields.name: MIN_BURNBACK
fields.doc:
The least time the arc burns back with the wire stopped before it is switched off, in seconds. With none, wire and
arc would stop at the same instant and the wire would stick in the pool (the arc model does not flag that, a real
supply's burnback does it).

fields.name: straight
fields.doc: A plan for one straight seam from `start` to `stop`.

fields.name: start
fields.doc: Where the path starts and ends.

fields.name: length
fields.doc: The length of the segments together.

fields.name: reversed
fields.doc: Reverse travel and its push angle while keeping the wire's component in the faces' cross-section.

fields.name: transformed
fields.doc: The plan in the frame `frame_T_this` leads to: its poses become `frame_T_this * pose`.

types.name: WeldRunner
types.doc:
Arm motion and process control for welding one seam. RobotKit names the work; ProcessKit implements it
(`processkit.WeldingPlanRunner`, a MotionKit program driven by a process run), so RobotKit itself stays free of
both, as with `HandlingRunner`. It works through the robot alone: the torch's channels and the motion, and the
welder's reading, which the caller hands in each tick from whatever reports it.

fields.name: run
fields.doc: Starts welding `plan`, in the arm's base frame.

fields.name: update
fields.doc: Advances `dtSeconds` with the welder's latest `reading`.

fields.name: completed
fields.doc: The seam is welded and the torch is clear of it.

fields.name: restarts
fields.doc: How many times the arc was lost and the weld restarted.

types.name: WeldSeam
types.doc:
Welds one seam with the robot's torch. `seam` gives the plan in the map frame, read when the skill starts so it
follows the workpiece wherever it stands; the robot's place comes from `localization`, and its base must stand
still meanwhile. The runner brings the torch in, strikes and holds the arc, travels the seam, fills the crater, ends
the arc and retracts, restarting with an overlap if the arc is lost on the way; this skill only starts it and
reads the outcome on the torch's `tool_weld` sensor, as `HandlePart` does the vacuum's. The weld has succeeded
when the runner is done and the welder reports its arc out and no fault.

fields.name: SENSOR_TIMEOUT
fields.doc: How long the sensor may stay silent before the weld is given up, in seconds.

types.name: WeldSegment
types.doc:
One straight piece of a weld path: the poses of the wire tip at its two ends (+Z along the wire out of the torch, +X
along the direction of travel), in the plan's frame. The torch holds its orientation from `start` to `stop`. `name` says
which seam it lies along, for messages; `open`, when given, is the unit vector pointing out of the corner into the open
side (the bisector of the two faces' outward normals), along which the torch can also come in and leave.

types.name: GroundedWork
types.doc:
Grounded work made of convex solids, each carried by a body whose pose is read when asked, so the work
follows what carries it (a fixture on a moving base, a workpiece on a positioner).

fields.name: addWork
fields.doc: Runtime metal, whose geometry changes as it is deposited.

fields.name: add
fields.doc: Adds a solid whose vertices are in the frame of the body `pose` reports.

fields.name: addFixed
fields.doc: A solid fixed in the world.

fields.name: ray
fields.signature: (ox:Float, oy:Float, oz:Float, dx:Float, dy:Float, dz:Float, range:Float):Float

types.name: ToolContactProfile
types.doc: Radial contact patch of the screwdriver's bit-front contact switch, in metres.

types.name: WeldArcConfig
types.doc: The welder behind a torch: the supply's limits and the wire.

types.name: WeldArcInput
types.doc: What the model is told each step.

types.name: WeldArcModel
types.doc:
The electrical and process behaviour of a MIG/MAG welder, without any geometry: it is told how far the wire
tip is from the grounded work and what the controller commands, and says what the circuit does. Time
advances by `step`, so the model is deterministic and runs the same under any physics backend.

**Arc.** With the arc commanded on, the supply ready and the wire fed (`MIN_WIRE_SPEED`), the arc strikes when
the work is within `STRIKE_REACH` ahead of the wire tip, as the wire advances to scratch it, and is
established after `IGNITION_DELAY` of that. It burns while the arc length stays within `MAX_ARC_LENGTH`. The arc
length is the tip's distance from the work plus `NOMINAL_ARC_LENGTH`: a torch held at its tool point, the
programmed wire tip on the joint, burns an arc of nominal length. It goes out when the torch is pulled away
(arc lost, a fault), when the arc is commanded off, or when the wire stops feeding (burnback).

**Current** follows the wire speed by the burn-off law: the wire melts at a rate
`MR = α·I·A0/A + β·l·I²·(A0/A)²` (mm/s), the first term the heat at the arc root, the second the resistive
heating of the stickout `l` (mm) of wire of cross-section `A` (mm²), against the reference 1.2 mm wire's `A0`. α
and β are calibrated for mild steel solid wire to 250 A at 8 m/min, 1.2 mm wire, 15 mm stickout. The supply
cannot deliver more than its rating, so the current is capped there. For a given wire speed the current is the
positive root of that quadratic.

**Voltage** is the setpoint plus `ARC_VOLTAGE_GRADIENT` per millimetre of arc length beyond the nominal, so
lifting the torch raises it, never below `MIN_ARC_VOLTAGE`. With the arc off it is the sensing voltage
(`SENSE_VOLTAGE`, open circuit), which collapses to nothing when the wire touches the work.

**Touch** closes while the wire tip touches grounded work (within `TOUCH_TOLERANCE`) with the arc off and the
supply ready.

**Faults** latch and clear once the arc is commanded off (a wire stuck in the pool also needs the torch freed).
- `NoArc`: the arc was commanded for `NO_ARC_TIMEOUT` without striking;
- `ArcLost`: the arc went out while commanded on, other than by burnback;
- `WireStuck`: the arc was commanded off while the wire touched the work and was still feeding, so no burnback
freed it. A process avoids it by stopping the wire a moment before the arc, or by retracting.
A fault turns the arc off.

**Power** drawn from the mains is the arc power divided by the supply's efficiency: `I·U/η`.

Units: metres for distances, m/min for wire speed, volts, amperes, watts, seconds.

types.name: WeldBead
types.doc:
The weld metal laid along one straight seam, as the wire actually deposited it. It is told every step whether the arc
is established, how fast the wire feeds and where the wire tip is, and keeps the metal deposited at each station along
the seam. Nothing here is a plan: the bead is what the torch did, so a stop, a slow-down, a restart's overlap or an
arc that went out show in it.

**Deposition.** The wire melts into the joint as it is fed: in `dt` seconds the arc melts `wireSpeed · A · dt` of wire
(`A` the wire's cross-section), and `depositionEfficiency` of it reaches the bead, the rest being spatter and fume. The
efficiency is a property of the wire and its gas, given with the wire (the scene's torch block).
That metal goes to the station of the seam the wire tip is over. Moving at travel speed `v`, a station receives the
metal of the time the tip is over it, so the cross-section is the deposition rate over travel speed:
`area = wireSpeed · A · efficiency / v`. Standing still piles it into one station, as a crater does.

**Section.** A fillet's section is a triangle against the two faces, an equal-leg one here: legs of
`sqrt(2 · area)`, a straight face (a concave or convex profile would shift the leg for the same area, by a few
percent). `leg(i)` is that leg at station `i`, and the achieved leg of a weld is a result compared with the leg the
weldment asked for.

The seam is cut into stations of `BIN` metres. The tip counts as welding it when it is within `REACH` of the seam
line and not more than `OVERRUN` past either end; metal deposited while it is elsewhere (an arc held in the air above
the work, say) is `stray`. Lengths are metres, wire speed metres per minute, the wire's diameter millimetres.

types.name: WeldBeadWork
types.doc: Deposited station triangles extruded along the seam; shared by sensing and clearance.

fields.name: vertices
fields.doc: The actual station prism in the bead frame, or no vertices before metal is deposited.

fields.name: ray
fields.signature: (ox:Float, oy:Float, oz:Float, dx:Float, dy:Float, dz:Float, range:Float):Float

types.name: WeldBodyPose
types.doc: Where a body is in the world: a position and an xyzw rotation, as a link pose is.

types.name: WeldChannelPolicy
types.doc:
Whether each of a welder's channels keeps its output through a commanded stop or an aborted motion. The arc is off
and the wire stopped at their safe values, and neither keeps its output: a robot that stops must not leave an arc
burning or the wire feeding. The voltage setpoint harmlessly keeps its value, so a restarted process need not write
it again. Faults and emergency stops take every channel to its safe value regardless.

types.name: WeldChannels
types.doc:
The channels a welding torch is worked by, with their safe values and stop policy (`WeldChannelPolicy`): whatever stops
the robot, the arc goes off and the wire stops. Every torch tool a robot is set up with has them, so the runtime
enforces it for every way of running the robot.

types.name: WeldContract
types.doc: Device-neutral welding units, feedback layout and safe output declarations.

fields.name: declarations
fields.doc: Wire speed is m/min, voltage is V; an optional job is a nonnegative integer encoded as an analog value.

types.name: WeldFault
types.doc: Why a welder stopped, as the `tool_weld` sensor's fault code carries it. `WeldSensor.faultMessage` puts it in words.

fields.name: NoArc
fields.doc: The arc was commanded and did not light within the timeout.

fields.name: ArcLost
fields.doc: The arc went out while it was commanded on: the torch was pulled away, or the supply dropped out.

fields.name: WireStuck
fields.doc: The arc was switched off with the wire still feeding while it touched the work, so it froze in the pool.

types.name: WeldPathBead
types.doc:
The weld metal laid along a path of straight seams, as the wire deposited it: one `WeldBead` per segment, each with
the faces' normals of its own seam (the sides of a tube lie between different faces). Each step the metal goes to
the segment whose line the wire tip is nearest, among those the tip is over (`WeldBead.over`); at a corner the tip is
on both lines and the earlier segment keeps it until the tip has left that one's end. Metal the tip puts down
while it is over no segment is `stray`.

fields.name: deposited
fields.doc: Metal in all the beads, in cubic metres.

fields.name: stray
fields.doc: Metal that went anywhere but into a seam, in cubic metres.

fields.name: new
fields.doc: `starts`, `stops` and `normals` (two per segment) give the segments in order, in one frame.

fields.name: step
fields.doc: Advances `dt` seconds with the arc `established` (or not), the wire fed at `wireSpeed` m/min, its tip at `tip`.

fields.name: covered
fields.doc: Stations with metal, over all the segments.

fields.name: length
fields.doc: The length of the seams together, in metres.

fields.name: gaps
fields.doc: Bare stretches inside a segment's metal, and a segment left with none when a later one has some.

types.name: WeldReading
types.doc: One reading of a welder: what a `tool_weld` sensor frame carries.

types.name: WeldSensor
types.doc:
The `tool_weld` sensor: one frame of six values in a fixed order, so a reading is a consistent snapshot of
the circuit rather than six sensors sampled at different moments. A real welder (a retrofit I/O board or
a Modbus supply) publishes the same frame.

fields.name: faultMessage
fields.doc: The fault code in words, or null for none.

fields.name: valid
fields.doc: Whether `values` is a well-formed frame: six finite values, flags 0 or 1, a known fault code, no negative current or power.

types.name: WeldWork
types.doc:
The grounded work of a weld: the metal the circuit returns through, which is all an arc can strike
to. Points and rays are in the world frame, in metres.

fields.name: distance
fields.doc: How far the point is from the nearest grounded surface: negative inside the metal, positive infinity with none.

fields.name: ray
fields.signature: (ox:Float, oy:Float, oz:Float, dx:Float, dy:Float, dz:Float, range:Float):Float
fields.doc: Where the ray from `o` along the unit vector `d` first meets grounded metal within `range`, or positive infinity.

types.name: BucketSweep
types.doc:
Approximate material removal for a `HeightMap`: a straight cutting-edge
sweep from `from` to `to`, `halfWidth` wide, lowers every grid vertex
within that capsule footprint (perpendicular distance to the swept
segment `<= halfWidth`) that is currently higher than `edgeHeight` down to
`edgeHeight`. An optional design map clamps the cut at each vertex so the
sweep cannot remove material below design, and an optional footprint limits
the cut to the work region. The reported volume is the integrated height-map
difference before and after the sweep, rather than a per-vertex estimate.

types.name: BucketSweepResult
types.doc: Outcome of one `BucketSweep.apply` call.

types.name: CoverageMap
types.doc:
A regular grid over a `WorkSurface`'s boundary bounding box, tracking
which cells a process-on TCP footprint has covered. Each cell is
classified once at construction, by its center, as `allowed` (inside the
boundary and no exclusion), `excluded` (inside the boundary and inside an
exclusion), or neither (outside the boundary entirely).
`coverageFraction` reports allowed coverage; `exclusionCoverageFraction`
reports whether the process ever touched an excluded cell, independent of
simply falling outside the boundary.

fields.name: markFootprint
fields.doc: Marks every cell whose center lies within `radius` of `center` as covered, regardless of classification.

fields.name: markSweep
fields.doc: Marks the footprint at evenly-spaced samples (at most `stepSize` apart) along a straight move.

fields.name: exclusionCoverageFraction
fields.doc: Fraction of excluded cells the process footprint nonetheless touched; should be zero.

fields.name: excludedCellsTouched
fields.doc: Excluded cell centers a footprint nonetheless touched; should be empty.

fields.name: uncoveredCells
fields.doc: Allowed cell centers that remain uncovered.

types.name: DeviationMap
types.doc:
A regular grid over a `WorkSurface`'s boundary bounding box (mirroring
`CoverageMap`'s grid), accumulating the mean signed out-of-plane deviation
(surface-vs-design, meters) reported for each cell. A caller adds samples
already expressed in the surface's own local plane (`x, y` in-plane,
`deviation` the signed distance from the design/registered plane at that
`x, y` — e.g. a registered point cloud's residual `z` after removing the
rigid registration correction), so a smooth bow shows up as a spatial
pattern across cells rather than a single scalar.

types.name: DigCyclePlan
types.doc: A planned dig cycle's `Toolpath`, plus the sweep to apply to a `HeightMap` once it executes.

fields.name: cuttingEdgeFrom
fields.doc: Cutting-edge path used by the engaged toolpath, inset from trench walls.

types.name: DigCyclePlanner
types.doc:
Plans one excavator dig cycle (entry -> cut -> curl -> lift -> swing ->
dump) as a `Toolpath`, for a 4-DOF chain shaped like `slew (Z) -> boom (Y)
-> stick (Y) -> bucket (Y)`: because every non-slew joint turns about a
parallel axis, the chain's *only* reachable tip orientations are
`Rz(slew) * Ry(totalPitch)` (see `poseAt`, and ARCHITECTURE.md's
"Simulated excavator (M12)" section for the derivation from
the joint-frame composition order in `kinematicskit.KinematicSnapshot`). Every waypoint this
planner emits sets its orientation from `poseAt`, so it always lies
exactly on that manifold; the generic numerical IK
(`Manipulator.solveIkForTcp`) then converges to near-zero
position *and* orientation error with no weighting or closed-form solver
of its own, since a target already on the manifold leaves the "extra" two
6-DOF error components at zero by construction.

fields.name: poseAt
fields.doc: `Rz(atan2(y, x)) * Ry(pitch)`: the one tip orientation this chain shape can reach at `(x, y)`.

fields.name: planCycle
fields.signature: (frameId:String, entry:Point2, exit:Point2, groundZ:Float, depth:Float, clearanceZ:Float, dump:Point2, dumpZ:Float, bucketHalfWidth:Float, digPitch:Float, curlPitch:Float, dumpPitch:Float, feedRate:Float, ?swingSteps:Int):DigCyclePlan
fields.doc:
`entry`/`exit` are the cutting edge's XY (chain-base frame) at the start
and end of the cut; `groundZ` the terrain elevation there before this
cycle; `depth` how far below `groundZ` to cut. The bucket lifts clear at
`clearanceZ`, swings through `swingSteps` intermediate waypoints (each
built from `poseAt`, so the swing stays on the reachable manifold) to
`dump` at `dumpZ`, then opens to `dumpPitch`. Returns both the
`Toolpath` and the full swept-segment parameters
(`BucketSweep.apply(heightMap, sweepFrom, sweepTo, sweepHalfWidth,
sweepEdgeHeight)`) a caller applies once the cycle's execution succeeds.
The engaged cutting edge is inset by half the bucket width at each
longitudinal trench wall, while the material sweep remains clipped to the
authored region. This keeps the tool out of the wall and accounts for the
whole bucket footprint in the terrain update.

types.name: EarthworkRegion
types.doc:
A grading task: an `existing` and `design` `HeightMap` sharing one grid
(see `HeightMap.ensureSameGrid`), exclusion polygons (in the height maps'
own XY plane, e.g. an existing utility or structure to leave undisturbed),
and the grade tolerance a vertex must be within to count as "at grade".

fields.name: deltaAt
fields.doc: Signed cut (positive)/fill (negative) still required at a grid vertex to reach design grade.

fields.name: isAtGrade
fields.doc: A vertex is "at grade" once its |existing - design| delta is within tolerance, or it is excluded.

fields.name: gradeFraction
fields.doc: Fraction of grid vertices (excluded ones count as at grade) currently at grade.

fields.name: worstVertex
fields.doc: The worst-graded (largest |delta|), non-excluded vertex still needing work; null if all are at grade.

fields.name: remainingVolume
fields.doc: Remaining cut/fill volume, ignoring any grid cell touching an exclusion.

types.name: HeightMap
types.doc:
A regular grid of terrain elevation samples in a named frame (mirroring
`CoverageMap`/`DeviationMap`'s grid conventions), used by the excavator
milestone. Unlike `CoverageMap`, samples live at grid *vertices*
(`columns x rows` points spaced `cellSize` apart, starting at
`(originX, originY)`), which is what makes `bilinearSample` and
`volumeBetween`'s per-cell trapezoidal average well defined. Elevation is
mutable state (like `CoverageMap.covered`), not an immutable value type:
it models terrain that a `BucketSweep` physically lowers over time.

fields.name: lowerTo
fields.doc: Lowers a vertex to `z` if it is currently higher; no-op (never raises terrain) otherwise.

fields.name: setElevation
fields.doc: Sets a vertex's elevation directly (raises or lowers); used to author fixtures.

fields.name: copy
fields.doc: Returns an independent mutable copy with the same grid and elevations.

fields.name: bilinearSample
fields.doc: Bilinearly-interpolated elevation at an arbitrary in-plane point; throws outside the grid's extent.

fields.name: contains
fields.doc: Whether `(x, y)` falls within this grid's extent.

fields.name: volumeBetween
fields.doc:
Cut (existing above design)/fill (existing below design) volume between
two height maps sharing the same frame and grid geometry. Each of the
`(columns - 1) x (rows - 1)` grid cells contributes the average of its
four corners' signed `existing - design` difference times the cell's
plan area; `skipCell`, if given, omits a cell entirely (its lower-left
vertex indices), e.g. for `EarthworkRegion` exclusions.

types.name: Point2
types.doc: Immutable x/y coordinate in a WorkSurface's own plane, meters.

types.name: Polygon2
types.doc: Immutable simple polygon in a WorkSurface's own XY plane; vertices counter-clockwise.

fields.name: scanlineIntervals
fields.doc: X-intervals (ascending, non-overlapping) where the horizontal line at `y` is inside this polygon.

fields.name: contains
fields.doc: Point-in-polygon test (even-odd rule); boundary points are treated as outside.

fields.name: containsOrWithin
fields.doc: Point-in-polygon with a finite distance tolerance around the boundary.

types.name: PolygonBounds
types.doc: Axis-aligned bounding box of a Polygon2, in its own plane.

types.name: Provenance
types.doc: Traces a WorkSurface back to the design element (and derivation kind) it came from.

types.name: RasterToolpathGenerator
types.doc:
Boustrophedon raster over a `WorkSurface`'s boundary minus its exclusions,
clipped row by row with polygon scanline intersection. Each exclusion is
expanded by the tool radius before its intervals are removed. The expanded
intervals are the exact horizontal slices of the polygon's Minkowski sum
with a disk: the polygon interior, an offset strip around every edge, and a
disk around every vertex are unioned. This handles rotated and concave
exclusions without relying on their bounding boxes. The tool is off while
transiting between rows and across exclusion gaps; lead-in/lead-out points
bracket the whole path off-process. Curved surfaces are out of scope;
geometry stays planar.

types.name: SourceKind
types.doc: Where a WorkSurface's geometry came from.

types.name: VolumeResult
types.doc: Cut/fill volume in cubic meters, e.g. from `HeightMap.volumeBetween`.

fields.name: net
fields.doc: Net volume: positive means net cut (material to remove), negative means net fill.

types.name: WorkSurface
types.doc:
A planar region of design/observed/work geometry to run a surface process
over. `frameId` is the frame this surface is registered against (e.g. a
BIM wall's frame or a robot's world frame); `surfaceFrameId` names this
surface's own local plane frame (+Z outward normal), and `frame_T_surface`
is the `frameId -> surfaceFrameId` edge a caller registers into a
`FrameTree3` (see `frameEdge()`). `boundary`/`exclusions`, and every
`Toolpath` a generator builds over this surface, are expressed directly
in `surfaceFrameId`.

fields.name: frameEdge
fields.doc: The `frameId -> surfaceFrameId` registration edge, ready for `FrameTree3.add`.

types.name: WorkSurfaceId
types.doc: Stable work surface identity; never a runtime index.
